Full-time · Contractor · Remote · Monthly salary: $4,000 to $5,500 USD Worldwide, with partial overlap with Pacific Time required  About the role  You coordinate fund operations in the back office of  Kinship Ventures , engaged through Trolley. You own the records behind every investor, deal and relationship, so the fund's memory lives in shared systems and not in personal inboxes. You take the admin load off the Fund Principal so he can focus on sourcing, allocations and raising. You prepare and recommend, and a senior person validates statements, updates and anything sent to investors; you never sign, approve payments or give legal or tax answers.  You report to the Finance Lead, with a dotted line to the Fund Principal, and work closely with the Managing Partner, the Bookkeeper and the Production and Marketing team.  About Moj and Trolley  Moj Mahdara is an entrepreneur and investor. She is Co-Founder and Managing Partner of  Kinship Ventures , the venture platform she launched alongside Gwyneth Paltrow, and the founder of Trolley. Before Kinship, Moj was CEO of Beautycon Media, the global festival and media company built at the intersection of beauty and pop culture.  Trolley is a fast-growing creative operations company delivering high-impact digital and marketing solutions. We work with high-profile clients and founder-led brands to strategize, produce and optimize content that drives engagement, brand visibility and business growth. Our team combines strategy, design, production and performance analysis, and we work AI-first. We are a fast-moving, collaborative remote team that values respect, teamwork and open communication.  What you will own  
 A complete file in Drive for every investor and SPV, from first capital call to latest K-1, with gaps flagged with an owner and a date. 
 The Fund I close checklist, from subscription documents, side letters, KYC and AML to wires and countersignatures, complete by the January 15, 2027 close. 
 The investor tracker and Real Deal CRM, with every touchpoint logged within one business day and a one-page pipeline snapshot ready before the daily partner call. 
 Capital calls and fund administrator requests, with notices sent, receipts tracked, wire instructions verified by phone and every request list cleared. 
 K-1 distribution, the compliance calendar, and the statement and investor update calendar, so every filing and update goes out on time after validation. 
 Data rooms, Carta, entity records and insurance summaries kept current, with one dated final version of each document and access approved and logged. 
 The investor inbox, with routine replies within one business day, plus expense and management fee tracking by entity. 
 A short weekly update, an SOP for every recurring task, AI workflows that save time, and support for the Finance Lead on Trolley finance operations as capacity allows. 
  Who you are  
 You come from fund operations or financial operations, such as a fund administrator, VC or PE fund, family office, or an accounting, audit, legal operations or investor relations operations team serving funds. 
 You have hands-on experience in at least two of these: capital calls, investor records, K-1 or tax document distribution, investor onboarding, fund administrator requests and entity paperwork. 
 You have kept a system of record others trusted, such as a CRM, investor database, cap table or data room, and you check your work before you report it. 
 You work comfortably in Google Sheets or Excel, read a capital account statement and check receipts against commitments. 
 Advanced written and spoken English. 
 Advanced use of AI: it is already part of how you work every day. 
  Nice to have  
 Spanish, or experience with a US-based leadership team in a remote contractor setup. 
 Hands-on use of Carta, Real Deal or a similar CRM, DocuSign and a data room platform. 
 Experience supporting a fund close, placement agent work, investor relations, expense and management fee tracking, or plain-language summaries of insurance policies and agreements. 
  This role is not  Not an investment analyst, fundraiser, controller, signer, payment approver, legal or tax advisor, or HR role.  How we hire  The stages depend on the case, and usually include:  
 A 15-minute interview 
 A skills test 
 A 30-minute interview with the manager 
 A final interview with Moj, our CEO 
  Equal opportunity  Trolley is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and make hiring decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability or any other protected status. We are not considering applications from agencies or recruiters at this time.  We use AI tools to help organize and shortlist applications. A person reviews every application before any rejection and makes every final decision.  Originally posted on  Himalayas

jobs.description: Customer Service Executive — uPhone  uPhone · Fully remote (work from anywhere) · Full-time · Apply to   Posted 18 November 2026 · Open until 17 January 2027  Fully remote — work from anywhere in the world, with no country restriction. Compensation is competitive and negotiable based on experience.  About uPhone  uPhone is an eSIM marketplace built for modern travellers, available at  (). The service is operated by Targa Limited, a company registered in Hong Kong. The team is small, remote-first, and based across Europe and Asia.  uPhone was founded on a simple belief: staying connected abroad should not be expensive, complicated, or stressful. The company sources eSIM data plans from multiple suppliers across 150+ countries so travellers can get a fair price — without hidden fees, locked contracts, roaming charges, or the plastic waste of a physical SIM card.  What uPhone eSIM is, in practice: an eSIM is a digital SIM profile built into the phone. Customers choose a country, regional, or global data plan (5,000+ plans are listed, including unlimited-data options and a Globetrotter plan covering 150+ countries on one eSIM), pay securely (card or PayPal; other methods, including crypto on the Crypto eSIM checkout, are listed on the site), and receive a QR code by email — typically within seconds. They scan it in iPhone or Android settings and can be connected in under two minutes, with no store visit. The physical SIM stays in the phone, so the home number remains available. Plans are data-only; calls and texts abroad are made over apps such as WhatsApp, FaceTime, or iMessage. Monthly and yearly plans are available for trips of 30 days or more. Plans are listed from about $2, with no contract.  uPhone publishes 24/7 customer support via live chat and email (the help centre cites a typical response time under two minutes), a 30-day unused-eSIM refund if the QR code has not been scanned and the eSIM has not been installed or activated, and a rating of 4.8/5 from 50,000+ travellers who trust the service.  Company values, as stated on the About Us page: transparency (what you see is what you pay), simplicity (purchase to connected in under two minutes), reliability (24/7 support and a clear refund policy), and sustainability (digital eSIMs mean zero plastic waste).  The role  We are hiring a Customer Service Executive to be a frontline point of contact for travellers using uPhone eSIM.  You will help customers choose a plan, install their eSIM, troubleshoot connection issues, and understand refunds and top-ups — over live chat and email. Many conversations happen just before a flight or just after landing, so clear, accurate, and calm help matters. This is a fully remote, full-time role — you can work from anywhere in the world. Support is published as 24/7, with a typical response time under two minutes, so this role includes shift work. That may include evenings, nights, weekends, or public holidays, as agreed with the team.  You do not need to be an engineer. You do need to follow documentation, explain technical steps in plain language, and know when to escalate.  Responsibilities  - Respond to customer questions on live chat and email within the team's service standards, aiming to protect the published typical response time of under two minutes.  - Help travellers choose an appropriate country, regional, or global plan (including unlimited and longer-stay monthly or yearly options) and explain what is included: uPhone plans are data-only; the physical SIM and home number can stay in the phone; calls and texts go through apps such as WhatsApp, FaceTime, or iMessage.  - Walk customers through purchase, QR-code delivery, installation on iPhone and Android, and when to activate (profiles can be installed before travel; data should usually be turned on at the destination so validity starts when it is needed).  - Troubleshoot common issues using the documented playbooks: device compatibility, carrier locks, APN settings, activation delays (typically under two minutes, occasionally up to around ten), coverage at the destination, top-ups, and exhausted data.  - Explain and process requests under the 30-day unused-eSIM refund policy (full refund only if the QR code has not been scanned and the eSIM has not been installed or activated). Escalating anything that does not fit the policy.  - Keep accurate notes, use approved macros, and flag repeating product, supplier, or documentation problems to the Customer Service Manager.  - Treat every traveller with patience and clarity, including people who are in a hurry, offline at an airport, or not confident with phone settings.  - Work in the team's live-chat and email tools, following the documented processes for each shift.  Requirements  - Experience in customer service, support, or a similar written-and-chat role, ideally in travel, e-commerce, telecom, or another digital consumer product.  - Excellent written English and the ability to give step-by-step instructions

Role Title:  Finance Research Expert   Role Type:  Contract   Location:  Remote  Required Skills:  
  Equity Research  
  FP&A  
  Corporate Finance  
  Accounting or Audit  
  Investor Relations  
  Credit Analysis  
  Opportunity Snapshot:  
   Time per task:  around 4 to 8 hours  
   Location:  Remote, worldwide  
   You’ll need:  Hands-on experience reading US SEC filings and familiarity with US GAAP  
   Your tasks:  Write finance research questions with a verified, sourced answer, and check each one against what AI models answer  
  Scope of Work:  
  You will work on questions about real US public companies. Each question points to information that sits in long filings or IR materials, or that requires comparing several of them to find the right answer.  
  Write questions that require finding a specific figure in a 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, proxy statement, earnings release or investor presentation.  
  Write questions where two documents show different numbers and the answer depends on knowing which one is correct (for example, original vs. restated figures, or adjusted vs. reported).  
  Pay attention to period and document version: the right fiscal year, the right filing, the latest amended version.  
  Test each question against current AI models and keep only the ones they answer incorrectly.  
  Rewrite questions when the wording allows more than one valid answer.  
  What we’re looking for:  
  Hands-on work with US filings in one of these backgrounds:   
  Equity research or investment analysis (sell-side or buy-side) covering US companies. Investment banking or corporate development. (M&A, equity capital markets), with experience in deal filings, prospectuses, ownership history and subsidiary structures.  
  Credit or restructuring analysis, with experience in credit agreements, bond terms and bankruptcy filings.  
  SEC reporting or audit. (Big 4 audit, corporate reporting), with experience in restatements, footnotes and how figures change across filings.  
  Corporate law or due diligence. (Securities law, KYC, investigations), with experience tracing entities, executives and related parties across records.  
  You should also be comfortable reading long filings, including footnotes and tables, and have clear written English.  
  How the selection process works:  
  Apply with your resume and a short profile.  
  Complete the finance interview. It is a short conversation about your experience with US filings and financial reporting. You don’t need to prepare or write anything. Finishing it is what moves your application forward.  
  Review. We check your experience against what the project needs.  
  Onboarding and first task. If selected, you get the guidelines and start with an initial task, which is reviewed before you continue.
